column1: # ZAP baseline ignore-list - the tripwire allow-list.
# Lines starting with # are comments; blank lines are ignored.
# THREE COLUMNS, AND THE THIRD IS NOT OPTIONAL IN PRACTICE.
# ZAP's loader refuses a line carrying fewer than two tab characters, and it rstrips the line
# before unpacking it into three, so a trailing tab passes the first check and fails the second.
# For an IGNORE the third column is a user message rather than a URL regex; a regex there only
# means anything when the level is OUTOFSCOPE. This file previously said otherwise and was written
# with two columns, which is why every scheduled scan from 2026-08-03 onwards died before it
# started. Seven weeks of red that said nothing about production.
# Each id below is a DOCUMENTED ACCEPTED RISK in docs/SECURITY-NOTES.md, confirmed present on
# production by a fresh scan (2026-07-28). IGNORE = the scan stays silent about it. With
# fail_action:true in zap-baseline.yml, ANY alert NOT listed here turns the run red. Known-accepted
# stays quiet; anything new is loud. To accept a NEW risk: add its id here AND a note in

column3: CSP unsafe-inline script/style: accepted risk 1, a zero-build app has no nonces
Subresource Integrity missing: accepted risk 2, Google Fonts serves UA-variant CSS
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy missing: accepted risk 3, no cross-origin isolation
Information Disclosure, suspicious comments: accepted risk 5, the repository is public
Re-examine Cache-control: accepted risk 4, single-file PWA caching strategy
Storable but Non-Cacheable: accepted risk 4, the same strategy
Modern Web Application: an informational detection, not a vulnerability
